title: alejandra alejandra…
editorial_note: The lowercase name and bare spatial debajo remain intact: the speaking self lies beneath the name yet returns to it in the final line.

title: The Wind Dies in My Wound…
text:
The wind dies in my wound.
+
+The night begs for my blood.
editorial_note: Mendiga is kept as an active begging rather than generalized hunger, making night a destitute presence at the wound.

title: Death Always Beside Me…
text:
Death always beside me.
+
+I listen to what it says.
+
+I hear only myself.
editorial_note: The distinction between listening and hearing is preserved; death’s speech closes into the speaker’s own voice without resolving whether it is solitary or prophetic.

title: Before
text:
musical forest
+
+
+the birds drew inside my eyes
+
+little cages
editorial_note: The image is left in its original reversal: birds do not escape cages but draw them within the perceiving eyes.

text:
I have been born so much
+
+and suffered doubly
+
+in the memory of here and there
editorial_note: He nacido tanto remains the deliberately strange born so much, allowing quantity, repetition, and excess to coexist with doubled suffering.

text:
like a poem aware
+
+of the silence of things
+
+you speak so as not to see me
editorial_note: Enterado becomes aware rather than merely informed; speech knowingly collaborates with the silence of things to avoid vision.

text:
to explain with words of this world
+
+that a ship departed from me carrying me away
editorial_note: The infinitive remains without a governing verb, while partió de mí holds both departure from the self and the self’s removal aboard the ship.

title: Hide Me from the Struggle with Words…
text:
Hide me from the struggle with words
+
+and extinguish the fury of my elemental body.
editorial_note: The plea binds linguistic combat to bodily fire; elemental retains both primal substance and uncontrollable force.
